newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT/Loctite rejected by 3 suitors.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT/Loctite rejected by 3 suitors.

text.p: Loctite Corp approached and was rejected by at least three possible "white knights," and takeover experts believe the company will not find an alternative to a $1.2 billion bid from Henkel KGaA.

Yet, they also see Henkel, a German chemical conglomerate, ultimately bumping its $57.75 per share offer by $2 to $3 per share to smooth its acquisition of the 65 percent of Loctite it doesn't already own.

Since receiving the offer, Loctite -- a leading maker of adhesives, sealants and coatings -- has approached and been spurned by DuPont Co, Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co and Ashland Inc, sources close to the situation said.

Hartford-based Loctite has been unable to draw a rescuer because a friendly buyer would be forced to contend with Henkel, which is a major shareholder and holds three of 12 Loctite board seats, the sources added.
Unilever and Morton International Inc were also mentioned as potential Loctite buyers, though it was unclear if they had been formally approached.

"It has been a quixotic search from the beginning because Henkel controls much of the the company and because Loctite on a stand-alone basis is a very nichey type of company," said Morgan Stanley analyst Mark Gulley.
All of the companies declined to comment.
"The search (for a friendly merger partner) not bearing fruit is no surprise at all," he said, expressing surprise that Henkel and Loctite had not yet agreed on a deal.
"I suppose Henkel will have to sweeten their offer, but not by a lot" in order to make Loctite succumb, Gully said.
A second analyst, who declined to be named, said: "With Henkel's 35 percent, it is pretty hard to find a white knight. My guess is that it ends up friendly."
Analysts said a winning bid would be in the $59 to $61 per share range.
Early Monday, Henkel said the U.S. government's waiting period for antitrust review of the transaction expired at 11:59 p.m. eastern time on Friday, November 22, 1986.
Henkel's tender offer is scheduled to expire at 1700 EST/ 2200 GMT on January 6, 1997, unless extended, it said.
In afternoon NYSE trade, Loctite shares fell 1/8 to 60.
On November 6, the Dusseldorf-based Henkel raised the bid to the current price from $56 per share.
